items.title: Melbourne woman suffers acute liver failure after using knock-off drug
items.description: Megan Hancocks bought a drug labelled as the peptide compound retatrutide in cash from a beautician. Within a week of her second dose, she was in acute liver failure.

items.title: Steve Irwin 'wouldn't have wanted this': Australia Zoo calls police on traditional owner
items.description: Traditional owner Alwyn Lyall says he felt "extremely upset and humiliated" when police asked him to leave Australia Zoo, where he was trying to see a crocodile he says was "wrongfully arrested" and taken from the wild.

items.title: First case of deadly H5 bird flu confirmed in Australia
items.description: The virus, found in a migratory bird in Esperance, raises concerns for the poultry industry despite Australia having spent years preparing for such a biosecurity breach.

items.title: A diabolical Iran deal reveals the Trump administration's delusions
items.description: Just as Netanyahu's claims to be able to influence Trump have now become a burden to him, Trump's limited capacity to influence Netanyahu spells just as much trouble for peace in the Middle East.

items.title: Could the 'bliss' trade set millions up for a comfortable retirement?
items.description: Does "bliss" — big lasting state support for financial entities deemed too big to fail — make the stock market a one-way bet?

items.title: Live: Paraguay star sent off under new rule, leads Türkiye in wild contest
items.description: A Paraguay star is sent off against Türkiye after covering his mouth during an altercation with an opponent. Follow live.

items.title: Transatlantic slave trade gravest crime against humanity, Juneteenth marks its end
items.description: Americans are commemorating Juneteenth months after a UN resolution on the transatlantic slave trade being the gravest crime against humanity.

items.title: Live: Knight sent off for alleged homophobic slur, Dolphins superstar sidelined
items.description: Newcastle back rower Asu Kepaoa is sent off during a NSW Cup game for an alleged homophobic slur. Meanwhile, in the NRL, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa is missing for the Dolphins' showdown with the Tigers due to a knee injury. Follow live.

items.title: One dead after huge fire at Dominican beach resort
items.description: A woman has been killed and nearly 1,700 tourists evacuated due to a large fire at a hotel in the Dominican beach resort town of Bayahibe.

items.title: Applause for Modra as Ricciuto describes optimism following surgery
items.description: Adelaide Crows fans clap at the sixth minute of the team's match against Melbourne to wish former number-six player Tony Modra well in his recovery from surgery following a serious truck crash.

items.title: Live: Crows hanging in with Demons in Adelaide Oval nailbiter
items.description: The Crows take on the Demons at Adelaide Oval, with a spot in the top four on the line, in the first of three games of Saturday football. Follow live.

items.title: Twin brothers born deaf hear their mum's voice for first time after epic surgery
items.description: An Australian-first eight hour surgical feat had one main purpose — for Artie and Jack to hear their mum's voice at the same time.

items.title: 'Everything's just so wrong': Inside the country town that turned to One Nation
items.description: In just a few short weeks, a small country town became One Nation heartland. It is a blueprint for how the party can turn Australia orange.

items.title: The immersive Indigenous language class where English is left at the door
items.description: After learning from Native American Yuchi families, Pertame elders and young mothers in Alice Springs are raising babies in a total immersion Language Nest and hope to extend the model into primary school.

items.title: Why these retirees won't give up the 3:30am starts and 14-hour shifts
items.description: When the alarm goes off at 3:30am in this freezing outback pit-stop, it's music to the ears of the volunteer bakers who happily spend their winters in a bakery like no other.

items.title: If you didn't do it at 40, do it at 60
items.description: For some women, the act of asking, "what might still be possible" — of refusing to accept that the most meaningful chapters are already behind them — might be its own kind of resistance.

items.title: This warming apple and miso pudding will have you back for seconds
items.description: Love a self-saucing pudding? This warm apple and miso version takes a classic to the next level

items.title: Zombie director Yeon Sang-ho says AI wants to 'fold' us into one
items.description: Train to Busan director Yeon Sang-ho is ringing the warning bell over AI's potential to strip humans of their individuality with his new zombie film Colony.

items.title: Sisters separated in Afghanistan are becoming Australian citizens
items.description: Five years ago, Adiba was separated from her sister Arya as she fled Afghanistan. Now the Ganji siblings have reunited in Melbourne and are on their way to obtaining Australian citizenship.

items.title: The women planting the seeds of a flower farm movement
items.description: Women looking for a new career or to invest in themselves are turning to micro flower farms, but pricing their blooms against industry giants can be challenging.

items.title: What Off Campus can teach us about centring women's pleasure
items.description: The college hockey romance has had millions of people swooning over its main characters and the messages around healthy relationships.

items.title: Mother holds onto hope her son's killer will be found after remote WA murder
items.description: The grieving mother of Josh Warneke, who was found dead on the side of a road in WA's remote Kimberley, has faced a long battle for answers. But how likely is it the 21-year-old's killer will be brought to justice?

items.title: What does it mean for a nation to be a 'monoculture'?
items.description: Pauline Hanson has called for Australia to reject multiculturalism and be "monocultural". So what does it involve and are there any nations overseas that show what it might look like in Australia?

items.title: 'He got that wrong': Schwarzer says selection mistakes cost Socceroos
items.description: The Socceroos will rue a missed opportunity after a dire first half against the USA, with Tony Popovic's selections at least partly to blame, says Mark Schwarzer.

items.title: Megastars bring new life to 'aging' country music
items.description: The country music genre has grown in popularity since the pandemic, spawning huge hits and an equally huge following in 2026 that nobody saw coming.
